title: Special Moves
concept: Castling, en passant, promotion: three secret handshakes.

glossary.definition: When a pawn reaches the last row, it turns into a queen, rook, bishop or knight. You'll almost always pick the queen.

summary: Push a free pawn toward promotion, take en passant the moment a pawn rushes past yours, and castle to get your king safe and your rook working.

narration: Black's knight grabs your bishop on d4. Greedy, and now it's far away from your h-pawn.
Pawn to h7. Your king guards it, and the knight is too far away to help.
Black's king hurries over, but it's one step too slow.
Pawn to h8 becomes a queen! That's promotion: reach the last row, and your pawn turns into any piece you like.

guided.hint: Your b-pawn is two steps from the last row. Can anything stop it?
guided.explanation: Push, push, promote! White's knight is too far away and the king arrives a move late, so your pawn becomes a queen on b1, with check.

guided.hint: Black's pawn just jumped two squares and landed right beside yours. That's your cue for a secret handshake.
guided.explanation: En passant! Black's pawn rushed from b7 to b5, right past yours. Your a5 pawn may take it as if it had moved only one square, landing on b6. Black makes a queen on f1, but your king takes her, and nothing can stop your b-pawn now.

wrong.g2f2: Grabbing the f2 pawn is natural, but en passant only works on the very next move. Use it now or lose it!

guided.hint: Your king is still on e1, and Black's queen is lurking on g1. Which special move gets your king out of there and brings a rook into the game?
guided.explanation: Castle queenside! Your king steps away to c1, and in the same move your rook lands on d1, guarding the whole back row. Black's queen grabs the bishop on f1, but your rook takes her: a bishop for a queen.
